content.subject: Nvidia Opens a Board Review. Heart Repair Advances in Mice. Climate Talks Begin.
content.preview_text: A corporate inquiry, an early heart repair study and the practical stakes of climate talks.
content.description: Nvidia investigates espionage allegations, researchers test heart repair in mice and COP31 opens, plus Egypt’s train collision and AI’s power equipment squeeze.
content.contents_extra: A deadly train collision, AI’s electricity squeeze, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Nvidia Opens a Board Inquiry as China Rejects Spying Allegations
paragraphs: Nvidia’s board announced an independent investigation Sunday into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence. AP reports that Huang will remain CEO during the review. The board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

China’s Foreign Ministry rejected the allegations Monday, calling them unsubstantiated. AP reports that Huang acknowledged an intimate relationship with a business executive. The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence identified the woman as gathering information for Beijing. That allegation remains the subject of the company’s inquiry.

stories.title: An Experimental Treatment Helps Injured Mouse Hearts Repair
paragraphs: A new mouse study offers an early route toward repairing heart muscle after a heart attack. Cambridge researchers report that temporary mRNA treatment stimulated heart cells to divide. Treated mice pumped about 10% more blood per heartbeat than mice receiving a mock treatment, according to the university.

The treatment temporarily activates proteins called Myc and cyclin T1. The study in Nature Cardiovascular Research describes repair and improved function in mice. Researchers still need studies in larger animals and then humans. These findings do not establish a safe or effective treatment for people with heart failure.

stories.title: Climate Talks Open With Pressure to Turn Promises Into Action
paragraphs: COP31 opened Monday in Antalya, Turkey, with delegates under pressure to implement climate commitments after another year of destructive weather. AP reports that Turkey is hosting while Australia leads negotiations. The conference runs through Nov. 20, with financing for poorer countries among the central disputes.

The energy debate also concerns how quickly countries can replace fossil fuels with electricity from cleaner sources. AP reports that outdated grids are obstructing renewable energy deployment. Installing generation alone is not enough when networks cannot absorb the supply. The talks face both diplomatic disagreements and physical infrastructure constraints.

stories.title: Egypt Investigates a Train Collision That Killed 7 Near Cairo
paragraphs: 2 trains collided Sunday in al Ayyat, south of Cairo. AP reports that 7 people were killed and at least 125 were injured, citing Egyptian authorities. Investigators arrived Sunday night. An initial inspection indicated that a moving train struck the rear of another train standing on the same track.

Rescuers and nearby residents pulled passengers from damaged carriages while emergency teams worked to clear the wreckage. Al Jazeera reported more than 125 injured and said the president ordered an urgent investigation. The reports do not establish responsibility for the collision.

deep_dive.title: Why AI Developers Are Searching for Used Turbines and Retired Jet Engines

photo.alt: Historic generator; contextual file photo, uploaded 2023.

paragraphs: What happened. Utilities and data center developers are searching for used gas turbines and engines adapted from aircraft. Reuters reports that delivery discussions for new U.S. equipment now center on 2030 and 2031. Its Monday analysis draws on brokers, service companies and suppliers. Developers are also reviving idle machinery rather than waiting for new units to arrive.

Why it matters. The shortage reaches beyond technology companies to utilities that need more generating capacity. Reuters cites worldwide turbine orders above 100 gigawatts against estimated global production capacity of 60 to 70 gigawatts. Wood Mackenzie puts average U.S. delivery waits at 6 years. Equipment prices have also risen sharply, according to the Tennessee Valley Authority.

What each side says. Equipment suppliers describe a busy secondary market and rising demand for refurbished machines. But analysts question how much relief it can provide. Enverus analyst Noor Qureshi told Reuters that limited surplus equipment is unlikely to offset a meaningful share of delays. Used turbines can also carry uncertain maintenance histories and limited remaining operating life.

What comes next. More manufacturing capacity is planned, but analysts still expect demand to exceed supply in 2028. Developers are assembling combinations of smaller machines and considering gas engines instead of turbines. Reuters reports that air permits and grid access remain separate obstacles. Securing a generator therefore does not by itself resolve every constraint on a project.

World view: New Zealand waits for final results. Incoming lawmakers are preparing for parliament while coalition negotiations await the final count; Reuters reports.
Saudi Arabia reports interceptions. Officials said falling debris damaged an Aramco building in Riyadh without casualties at the facility; AP reports.
A ship’s crew reaches safety. The UAE said it rescued 22 people after a cargo ship fire in the Sea of Oman; AP reports.
Ukraine reports power disruptions. Its deputy energy minister said Russian attacks left some consumers without electricity across 12 regions; Reuters reports.
Need to know: Congress returns Monday. Lawmakers face a government funding deadline in December before the new Congress takes office in January; AP reports.
Reservoir gains have limits. Lake Powell has risen more than 20 feet from September’s low, but the region remains in drought; AP reports.
Police announce a campus arrest. A suspect faces murder charges after a fatal shooting during Winston Salem State’s homecoming weekend; AP reports.
A Utah hearing addresses trial timing. A judge is expected to set a date in Charlie Kirk’s killing; the defendant denies guilt; AP reports.
Money & markets: Global markets edge upward. Monday’s recovery remained fragile as Nvidia’s investigation renewed pressure on technology shares; Reuters reports.
Inflation data arrive Tuesday. Investors await the U.S. consumer price report after strong employment figures reinforced expectations of higher interest rates; Reuters reports.
CTP expands toward Vietnam. The logistics property operator agreed to buy assets for $500 million, subject to regulatory approval; Reuters reports.
Evonik resists BASF’s approach. Handelsblatt reported renewed opposition after weekend talks; both companies declined to comment on the meeting; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: A chip materials acquisition advances. Mitsui Chemicals announced a 1.84 trillion yen JSR purchase with Development Bank of Japan investment; Reuters reports.
Researchers test PTSD screening. NYU says an AI tool flagged all 30 later cases within a study of 145 emergency patients; the university reports.
Clinical notes inform predictions. NYU’s Lang1 models were trained using records from more than 10 million patients to support healthcare decisions; the university reports.
Researchers unify physical simulations. MIT’s WorldParticle system models materials from sand to proteins using one AI architecture; MIT reports.
The score: Cincinnati wins in Madrid. Joe Burrow threw 3 touchdown passes as the Bengals beat Atlanta 34 to 17; Reuters reports.
Norris wins in Brazil. McLaren’s driver won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix as Mercedes secured the Formula One constructors’ title; Reuters reports.
Gauff opens with a win. Coco Gauff defeated Jessica Pegula in 3 sets at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells; Reuters reports.
Alcaraz takes the Paris title. Carlos Alcaraz beat Ben Shelton for his 5th title of the year; Reuters reports.
Life & culture: Godzilla leads the weekend. Godzilla Minus Zero opened with an estimated $31.6 million at North American theaters; AP reports.
Nepal celebrates dogs. Kukur Tihar brought garlands, ceremonial marks and treats honoring the animals’ loyalty; Radio Nepal reports.
Harlem prepares a new museum. The Urban Civil Rights Museum will explore Northern civil rights history through permanent and rotating exhibitions; AP reports.
Kabul’s fortress reveals earlier lives. Conservation at Bala Hissar has uncovered monastery remains, coins and ceramics; AP reports.

trivia.question: Which proteins does the experimental heart repair treatment temporarily activate?
trivia.explanation: A. Myc and cyclin T1. The mouse study temporarily activates these proteins to stimulate heart muscle cell division.

unresolved_points: Nvidia spying allegations are disputed; the independent inquiry has not established that company or national security secrets were compromised.
Cambridge research concerns mice, not a demonstrated therapy for patients.
Egypt injury reporting uses different lower bound wording: AP says at least 125; Al Jazeera says more than 125. Each source’s qualification is retained separately.
Two AI power deep dive URLs carry the same Reuters analysis, not independent confirmation. Credit remains Reuters.
The NYU PTSD press release does not provide a false positive rate. The brief states the sample and observed case detection, not general diagnostic accuracy.
Market direction is from the opened Reuters 12:01 UTC update, not a predicted opening or closing value.
The Harlem museum is upcoming. No claim is made that it already opened.
